request: does a 10-minute shower use more water than a bath?

beats.intent: A bath drawn as a tank holding 150 litres
beats.narration: A full bath holds about a hundred and fifty litres of water.
beats.code:
stage.title("Shower or bath?")
k = 0.02
base = -2.3
bath = Rectangle(width=1.4, height=150 * k, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.5).move_to([-4.6, base + 75 * k, 0])
stage.play(GrowFromEdge(bath, DOWN))
stage.add(bath)
stage.label(bath, "bath: 150 L", direction=UP, color=BLUE)
level = DashedLine([-5.5, base + 150 * k, 0], [-0.6, base + 150 * k, 0], color=BLUE)
stage.play(Create(level))
stage.add(level)

beats.intent: A shower tank filling 8 litres a minute, a minute counter reaching 10 at 80 litres
beats.narration: A shower pours out about eight litres a minute. Collect it: after ten minutes, eighty litres.
beats.code:
water = Rectangle(width=1.4, height=0.01, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.6).move_to([-2.2, base, 0], aligned_edge=DOWN)
stage.add(water)
counter = Text("0 min", font_size=30, color=GREEN).move_to([-2.2, 1.6, 0])
stage.add(counter)
for m in range(1, 11):
    stage.play(water.animate.stretch_to_fit_height(8 * m * k).move_to([-2.2, base, 0], aligned_edge=DOWN), Transform(counter, Text(f"{m} min", font_size=30, color=GREEN).move_to(counter)), run_time=0.25)
stage.add(water)
l80 = stage.label(water, "80 L", direction=RIGHT, color=GREEN)

beats.intent: The shower kept running until it reaches the bath line, at about 19 minutes
beats.narration: Keep the shower running and it only matches the bath at about nineteen minutes.
beats.code:
stage.play(FadeOut(l80))
stage.play(water.animate.stretch_to_fit_height(150 * k).move_to([-2.2, base, 0], aligned_edge=DOWN), Transform(counter, Text("about 19 min", font_size=30, color=GREEN).move_to(counter)), run_time=1.5)
stage.add(water)
stage.label(water, "150 L", direction=RIGHT, color=GREEN)

beats.intent: The tanks beside 8 × 10 = 80 L and 150 ÷ 8 ≈ 19 min
beats.narration: Eight times ten is eighty litres, about half a bath. A hundred and fifty divided by eight is about nineteen minutes, so a shower under nineteen minutes uses less.

request: how do you write 7/3 as a mixed number?

beats.intent: Seven pieces, each a third of a bar
beats.narration: Seven thirds means seven pieces, each one third of a whole.
beats.code:
stage.title("7/3 as a mixed number")
w = 1.0
pieces = VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=w, height=0.6, color=WHITE, fill_color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.6) for _ in range(7)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.15).move_to([-2.6, 1.4, 0])
stage.play(LaggedStart(*[FadeIn(p) for p in pieces], lag_ratio=0.15))
stage.add(pieces)
stage.play(*[FadeIn(Text("1/3", font_size=22).move_to(p)) for p in pieces])

beats.intent: Pieces fitted together in threes into two whole bars
beats.narration: Three thirds make a whole. Fit them together: the first six pieces make two whole bars.
beats.code:
wholes = VGroup(*[VGroup(*[Rectangle(width=w, height=0.6, color=WHITE, fill_color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.6) for _ in range(3)]).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0) for _ in range(2)]).arrange(DOWN, buff=0.3).move_to([-3.6, -0.6, 0])
stage.play(TransformFromCopy(VGroup(*pieces[:6]), VGroup(*[p for wh in wholes for p in wh])), run_time=1.5)
stage.add(wholes)
stage.label(wholes, "2 wholes", direction=LEFT, color=GREEN)

beats.intent: One third left over beside the two wholes
beats.narration: One piece is left over: one third.
beats.code:
left = Rectangle(width=w, height=0.6, color=WHITE, fill_color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.6).next_to(wholes, RIGHT, buff=0.6)
stage.play(TransformFromCopy(pieces[6], left))
stage.add(left)
stage.label(left, "1/3", direction=RIGHT, color=BLUE)

beats.narration: Seven divided by three is two remainder one: two whole ones and one third. Seven thirds is two and a third.

request: how fast is the Earth spinning at the equator?

beats.intent: The Earth as a circle with a point on the equator
beats.narration: Stand on the equator. The Earth turns once a day, carrying you with it.
beats.code:
stage.title("How fast does the Earth spin?")
c = np.array([-3, -0.3, 0])
earth = Circle(radius=2.2, color=BLUE, fill_opacity=0.2).move_to(c)
you = Dot(c + 2.2 * RIGHT, color=YELLOW, radius=0.12)
stage.play(Create(earth), FadeIn(you))
stage.add(earth, you)
stage.label(you, "you", direction=RIGHT, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: The point carried once round the circle, tracing the full 40 000 km equator
beats.narration: In one turn you travel the whole way round the equator: about forty thousand kilometres.
beats.code:
trail = TracedPath(you.get_center, stroke_color=YELLOW, stroke_width=4)
stage.add(trail)
stage.play(Rotate(you, angle=TAU, about_point=c), run_time=2.5, rate_func=linear)
stage.add(you)
stage.label(earth, "40 000 km in one turn", direction=DOWN, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: A 24-hour clock face beside the Earth: one turn takes 24 hours
beats.narration: And one turn takes twenty four hours.
beats.code:
clock = Circle(radius=0.8, color=WHITE).move_to([1.2, 1.2, 0])
hand = Line(clock.get_center(), clock.get_center() + 0.7 * UP, color=WHITE)
stage.play(Create(clock), Create(hand))
stage.play(Rotate(hand, angle=-TAU, about_point=clock.get_center()), run_time=1.5)
stage.add(clock, hand)
stage.label(clock, "24 hours", direction=DOWN)

beats.narration: Forty thousand kilometres in twenty four hours is about one thousand six hundred and sixty seven kilometres an hour: four hundred and sixty metres every second.

request: how far away is the horizon when you stand on a beach?

beats.intent: The curved Earth with a person standing on top, their height exaggerated
beats.narration: The Earth curves away beneath you. Stand on a beach with your eyes about one point seven metres up, drawn much taller here.
beats.code:
stage.title("How far is the horizon?")
O = np.array([-2.5, -3.7, 0])
R = 4.0
ground = Arc(radius=R, start_angle=15 * DEGREES, angle=150 * DEGREES, arc_center=O, color=BLUE)
E = O + (R + 1.0) * UP
eye = Line(O + R * UP, E, color=WHITE, stroke_width=6)
stage.play(Create(ground), Create(eye))
stage.add(ground, eye)
stage.label(eye, "h", direction=LEFT)

beats.intent: A line of sight from the eye just touching the Earth at the horizon H
beats.narration: Your line of sight just grazes the Earth at the horizon. Beyond that point the ground curves out of view.
beats.code:
th = np.arccos(R / (R + 1.0))
H = O + R * np.array([np.sin(th), np.cos(th), 0])
sight = Line(E, H, color=YELLOW)
stage.play(Create(sight))
stage.add(sight)
dot_h = Dot(H, color=YELLOW)
stage.play(FadeIn(dot_h))
stage.add(dot_h)
stage.label(dot_h, "horizon", direction=RIGHT, color=YELLOW)

beats.intent: Radii to H and to the eye forming a right triangle: R, R + h and the distance d, right angle at H
beats.narration: Join the centre of the Earth to the horizon and to you. The sight line meets the radius at a right angle, so it's a right angled triangle.
beats.code:
r_h = Line(O, H, color=GREEN)
r_e = Line(O, E, color=GREEN)
stage.play(Create(r_h), Create(r_e))
stage.add(r_h, r_e)
ra = RightAngle(Line(H, O), Line(H, E), length=0.25, color=WHITE)
stage.play(Create(ra))
stage.add(ra)
stage.label(r_h, "R", direction=RIGHT, color=GREEN)
stage.play(FadeIn(Text("d", font_size=30, color=YELLOW).move_to((E + H) / 2 + 0.35 * np.array([0.6, 0.8, 0]))))

beats.intent: The triangle beside d² = (R + h)² − R² ≈ 2Rh, d ≈ √(2 × 6371 × 0.0017) ≈ 4.7 km
beats.narration: Pythagoras: d squared is R plus h, squared, minus R squared, which is about two R h. With the Earth's radius, six thousand three hundred and seventy one kilometres, the horizon is only about four point seven kilometres away.
